items.heading: Nouns — Common & Proper
lines: The name we give in general to every person, animal, place or thing of the same kind is a common noun. Examples: boy, dog, city, pencil.
The name we give to a particular person, animal, place or thing is a proper noun. Examples: Aman, Tommy, Delhi.
Proper nouns always begin with a capital letter.

items.heading: Compound Nouns
lines: Some nouns are made up of more than one word — these are called compound nouns. They can be written as:
• one word, e.g. streetlight, cornflakes
• separate words, e.g. washing powder, baby tooth
• words joined with a hyphen, e.g. father-in-law, mother-in-law

items.heading: Nouns — Male & Female
lines: Words like 'girl', 'sister' and 'daughter' belong to the female group.
Words like 'boy', 'brother' and 'son' belong to the male group.

items.heading: Adjectives
lines: Words like happy, angry and sad are describing words — they tell us more about a noun. Example: Sana is a happy girl.
Describing words are called adjectives.

items.heading: Degrees of Comparison
lines: Adjectives describe nouns and pronouns, and can show comparison using three degrees.
1. Positive Degree — describes only one person or thing; no comparison is made. e.g. Rahul is tall. This is a beautiful dress.
2. Comparative Degree — compares two people or things, using '-er' or 'more' before the adjective. e.g. Rahul is taller than Shyam. This dress is more beautiful than that one.

3. Superlative Degree — compares more than two (three or more), using '-est' or 'most' before the adjective, usually with 'the'. e.g. Rahul is the tallest boy in the class. This is the most beautiful dress of all.
Short words usually take -er/-est (tall → taller → tallest). Longer words take more/most instead (comfortable → more comfortable → most comfortable).

items.heading: Commas & Full Stops
lines: A full stop is used at the end of a sentence.
Capital letters are used to begin a sentence, to write 'I', and to write a proper noun.
When there are more than two similar words in a sentence, we use commas to separate them. e.g. I have brought a chappati, some vegetables, salad and sweets.
A comma is also used to separate a noun used to address a person from the rest of the sentence. e.g. Dad, what are you having for dinner today?

items.heading: Apostrophe (Possessive Nouns)
lines: An apostrophe + 's' is used to show belonging. e.g. the boy's bag.
For plural nouns that already end in 's', we add only the apostrophe (no extra 's'). e.g. the students' books.

items.question: What was written on the notice put up by the giant? Why does the giant put up this notice?
items.answer: The notice put up by the selfish giant said 'TRESPASSERS WILL BE PROSECUTED'. The giant put up this notice because he doesn't want children to play in his garden.

items.question: How did the giant react on seeing the children play in his garden?
items.answer: The giant reacted angrily and did not allow the children to play in his garden.

items.question: Why was the giant happy at the end?
items.answer: The selfish giant was happy in the end because he had learnt the secret of happiness that lies in sharing and caring.

items.question: Do you think the trees were glad to have the children back? Give a reason for your answer.
items.answer: The trees were so glad to have the children back again that they had covered themselves with flowers and were waving their arms gently above the children's heads.

items.question: Why do you think spring forgets to visit the giant's garden?
items.answer: Spring forgets to visit the giant's garden because the giant's selfishness and the absence of children's laughter made the garden lack the joy and the happiness.

items.question: What does the poet mean by saying 'a child should never feel a fear' in nature?
items.answer: The poet means that nature is full of gentle and kind things that make a child feel safe and comfortable. There's no need for a child to feel afraid when surrounded by the caring elements of nature.

items.question: Which lines of the poem tell us that nature is caring and loving?
items.answer: The lines “The sunshine flickers through the lace, of leaves above my head, and kisses me upon the face like mother before bed,” convey that nature is caring and loving.

items.question: Where was the house situated that Sana saw? What did it have in its garden?
items.answer: The house that Sana saw was situated on a hill right in front of her own house. It had a golden fountain in its garden.

items.question: What did Sana wish to have in her own garden?
items.answer: Sana wished to have a golden fountain in her own garden.

items.question: Why did the fountain appear golden to Sana?
items.answer: The fountain appeared golden to Sana because of the rays of the sun shining on it. The sunlight made the fountain shine like gold.

items.question: Why was Sana shocked when she saw (a) the fountain on the hill, and (b) her own fountain from the house on the hill?
answer: (a) She was shocked because it was not as she had imagined — it wasn't made of gold and didn't have golden water.
(b) She was shocked because her own fountain appeared golden due to the sun's rays, which surprised her and changed her understanding of it.

items.question: What does the child wish for in the poem?
items.answer: The child wishes to have wings.

items.question: What does the child want to do with wings?
items.answer: The child wants to fly everywhere and see the world.

items.question: From where do you think the poet plans to gaze at the people on the earth?
items.answer: The poet imagines flying with wings and looking down at the people on the earth from the sky.

items.question: Reference to Context: “How happy we were there!”
answer: (a) Who are referred to as 'we'? — The children.
(b) Why does the speaker say so? — The giant had built a wall around his garden, so they had no place to play.

items.question: Personal Response: What have you learnt from this story?
items.answer: We should share our things with friends. This will make you happy.

items.question: Reference to Context: “The Sunshine flickers through the lace, Of leaves above my head, And kisses me upon the face Like Mother, before bed.”
answer: (a) Why does the poet compare the sunshine's touch to mother's love? — To show that both are gentle and loving.
(b) How does the poet feel about the sunshine? — Loved and cherished, like the warmth and comfort of a mother's love.

items.question: Reference to Context: “But, but… this fountain is not made of gold, nor does it have golden water.”
answer: (a) Which fountain is being talked about here? — The fountain in the house on the hill that Sana visited.
(b) Why did the speaker say so? — She expected it to be made of gold with golden water, but discovered that wasn't true.
(c) What did the speaker realise? — That her first impression about the fountain was incorrect.

items.question: Reference to Context: “I would listen to the clouds of sheep bleat / That graze on the blue.”
answer: (a) Who will graze on the blue? — Sheep.
(b) What do you understand by 'sheep bleat'? — The sound that sheep make.
(c) What does the poet mean by 'blue'? — The sky.

2. Date
3. Salutation
4. Body of the letter
5. Closing line
6. Name of the sender

items.heading: Worked example — letter to a cousin about summer vacation
lines: 2, Green Park
19 July 2026
Dear Cousin,
How are you? I am fine and hope you are doing well.

I want to tell you about my summer vacation. I visited my grandparents in the village. Every morning, I played with my cousins and helped my grandmother water the plants. In the evening, we went to the park and enjoyed eating ice cream.
I also read storybooks, drew pictures, and learned to ride a bicycle. We had a wonderful time together. My summer vacation was full of fun and happy memories.
I hope you also had a great vacation. Please write back and tell me about your holidays.
Yours lovingly,
Aarav

items.title: A Visit to the Library
items.text: Last Saturday, Rohan and his friends visited the library in their town. The library was full of books about animals, science, and adventure stories. A kind librarian helped them find books they liked. Rohan borrowed a book about dinosaurs, while his friends chose storybooks. Reading books in the library made them curious to learn more about the world.

questions.question: Where did Rohan and his friends go on Saturday?
questions.answer: Rohan and his friends visited the library in their town.

questions.question: How did the librarian help the children?
questions.answer: The librarian helped by finding books they liked.

questions.question: What did Rohan borrow from the library?
questions.answer: Rohan borrowed a book about dinosaurs.

questions.question: Fill in the blanks: The library was full of ___. The librarian was very ___.

items.title: Lina Bakes Chocolate Chip Cookies
items.text: Lina helped her mother bake chocolate chip cookies on Saturday afternoon. The kitchen smelled sweet and warm. They measured flour, sugar, butter and stirred the dough together. Lina rolled the dough into small balls and placed them on the tray. The oven timer beeped and they pulled the tray out carefully. Lina tasted a cookie and declared it the best cookie ever. She packed some in a jar for her father's snack the next day.

questions.question: What activity did Lina help with?
questions.answer: Lina helped her mother bake chocolate chip cookies on Saturday afternoon.

questions.question: What did Lina put into a jar?
questions.answer: She packed some cookies in a jar, having declared them the best cookies ever.

questions.question: Write rhyming words for: tray, sweet
Write the meaning of 'measured' and use it in a sentence.
questions.answer: measured — found the size or amount of something. “I measured the milk.”

items.title: Mina's Flower Garden
items.text: Mina visited a flower garden at the edge of town with her teacher. The garden had rows of pink roses, orange marigolds and violet tulips. A gentle breeze made the petals dance and butterflies landed on the blooms. Mina bent down to sniff a rose and felt its soft petals brush her fingers. Her teacher said, “Nature is full of wonders.” Mina nodded and pressed a flower between her notebook pages to remember this visit.

questions.question: Who visited the flower garden with Mina?
questions.answer: Mina visited the flower garden with her teacher.

questions.question: What flowers did she see?
questions.answer: She saw pink roses, orange marigolds and violet tulips.

questions.question: What did Mina press between her notebook pages?
questions.answer: Mina pressed a flower between her notebook pages.
